```shiploop-state
{
  "evidence_refs": [
    "original request, S1-S2 (the only source of requirements)",
    "intake exercise brief: repository empty, no tools or files, unattended run, implement nothing"
  ],
  "headline": "Mapped S1 (Python CLI that summarizes sales CSVs) and S2 (tests) to outcomes, boundaries and 5 open questions that each have an owner and a recorded default. Nothing blocks.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "Legend: [F] = fact stated by the request or exercise; [A] = assumption recorded as the default. || S1 OUTCOME [F]: a Python command-line tool reads CSV files of sales records and prints a summary of exactly three aggregates: total revenue, revenue per region, units per product. || S1 BOUNDARIES: Python and a command-line entry point are [F]. Everything else here is [A]. The tool uses Python 3 stdlib only (csv, argparse, decimal; no pandas). It takes one or more CSV paths as positional arguments and combines them into one summary. It prints plain text to stdout and reads the inputs without modifying them. It has no stdin mode, export files, charts, database, web UI or config file. It exits non-zero on unusable input. It is a stateless single-process batch tool, not an interactive product. The only actor is the shell user who runs it, with no identity or auth. There is no shared or persisted state, so nothing carries over between runs. Nothing is hidden from anyone and nothing is sent over a network. The runtime provides argv, stdout, the exit code and the stdlib csv module. These defaults rule out caching, history, auth and telemetry. || S2 OUTCOME [F]: automated tests are added alongside the tool. [A]: they run with one documented command and depend on S1's tool. They cover the three aggregates for one file and for several files, and header-only input. They also cover malformed rows, a missing file, and the CLI output and exit code. They use small fixture CSVs written to temp dirs, are deterministic, use no network or real data, and have no coverage threshold. || RUN BOUNDARIES: [F] the repository is empty (greenfield, with no conventions, CI, docs or sample CSVs to inherit). [F] the run is unattended and this stage implements nothing. [A] authority is limited to creating files in this repository; no push, publish, install, release or deploy is named or granted. [A] the consumer is the requester at a shell and the only entry point is the CLI. [A] this is not a continuation of an earlier run, so no prior-run recovery applies. RISKS: a wrong schema guess (highest); float rounding of money; silently skipped bad rows producing wrong totals; case or whitespace variants of region or product splitting one group into several. || OPEN QUESTIONS (no person answers during the run; discovery answers first, else the recorded default applies): Q1 CSV schema (S1): which columns and header names exist; whether revenue is a per-row column or derived as units x unit_price; whether region and product are names or codes. Answered by discovery, which must first look for sample CSVs, a data dictionary, an export job or its owner; the empty repo likely yields none. Default: a header row with region, product, units and revenue columns, matched after trimming and case-folding. Blocks: the parser, aggregation, fixtures and expected values in tests. Q2 numeric semantics (S1): currency, decimal places, currency symbols or thousands separators, negative units or revenue (returns). Answered by discovery of sample rows, else default: Decimal arithmetic, one implicit currency shown without a symbol, 2-decimal output, negatives summed as given, integer units. Blocks: parsing, output formatting, test expectations. Q3 bad or odd input (S1): blank or non-numeric fields, ragged rows, empty file, missing path, duplicate rows, BOM or encoding, delimiter. Answered by recorded default, since no evidence source is expected: strict mode reports file and line on stderr and exits non-zero with no partial summary; a header-only file gives zero totals; duplicates are kept; UTF-8 with BOM tolerated; comma delimiter. Blocks: error-handling design and negative tests. Q4 output format (S1): layout, ordering and number format of 'prints a summary'. Answered by discovery of any existing consumer or parser of the output (none expected), else default: three labeled plain-text sections with groups sorted alphabetically for determinism, and no JSON or CSV flag. Blocks: output code and golden-output tests. Q5 packaging, runner and Python version (S1, S2): tool name, layout, how to invoke, minimum Python, test framework. Answered by discovery of the run environment (interpreter version, whether pytest is installed), else default: a small stdlib-only package with a main(argv) function and a __main__ entry, run as `python -m <name> file.csv ...`, with unittest-style tests runnable by `python -m unittest` (pytest also collects them). Blocks: file layout, the test and verification commands. || DISCOVERY SOURCE HINTS (leads only, not verified facts; the request names no team, channel, internal site or private repository, so none is invented and no sensitive locator is recorded): the requester's team or workspace for a sample or real sales CSV export, its data dictionary or export job, and that export's owner (likely sales-ops, finance or BI; a guess); this repository (empty) and the run environment (python3 version, pytest availability). Ambiguous terms to pin down: 'sales records' (schema), 'revenue' (gross or net, per-row or derived, currency), 'region' (a column, or derived from country or state), 'product' (name or SKU), 'units' (quantity), 'summary' (format). Ask no questionnaire; if discovery finds nothing, proceed on the defaults above. || WHERE AND WHEN VISIBLE: the outcome becomes usable as source files (the CLI module and its tests) in this repository, runnable from the repo root with the commands fixed in Q5. Nothing is visible after intake, because this stage changes nothing. The files appear in the isolated run's checkout after the implement stage and are confirmed at verify. They reach the user's own source checkout only at the final return of the run; until then that checkout stays at its snapshot. No deployed target is named, so nothing is deployed, released or installed. The request grants creating the tool in the repository and nothing beyond that."
}
```
